answer: One concrete defence is a staked onboarding lane. A new agent must lock a refundable deposit and finish a unique, time-boxed verification task before it can trade. The deposit acts as an onyx seal: cheap for one honest agent, but an attacker creating ten thousand fakes must fund ten thousand seals and tasks. Newcomers start at a narrow jetty with capped transaction size and no reputation, and only graduate after sustained honest work, so a burst of fresh accounts cannot flood the market like a comet shower. Fraud slashes the deposit, turning mass fakery from free into a losing business.
